tests.name: test_linear_and_bilinear_generation_fold_the_same_fixed_truth
tests.claim: Generation folds linear (fold_truth) and bilinear (dy_central) observables from the same single fixed PDF truth, not a replica-ensemble statistic.
tests.actual: Pins cfg.FIXED_TRUTH_MEMBER==1 (a config value pin, unrelated in mechanism to the rest of the test). Checks fold_truth(operator, truth) against a direct numpy matrix-vector product, single-field operator only. Checks dy_central(dataset, truth, fields, 'pp') against a direct numpy outer-product contraction, through a real BilinearContribution whose kernel stub ignores nu/basis and returns a constant tensor, with field_A==field_B=='q' (one contribution, weight=1, no evolution). A closing assertion shows the fixed-truth law numerically differs from a replica-second-moment law on this fixture (measured 7-8%), which is what gives the direct-formula check teeth against that specific alternative.
tests.how: Both package=[closure_JAM_truth, closure_NNPDF_truth] parametrized cases execute byte-identical fold_truth/dy_central code (confirmed via diff of the two generate.py files); only the FIXED_TRUTH_MEMBER pin is separately re-checked per package, so the two cases are not materially different in mechanism.
tests.bar: assert_allclose default rtol=1e-7 atol=0 (x2, for the linear and bilinear identities); np.allclose default rtol=1e-5 atol=1e-8 (for the closing not-allclose check)
tests.catches: dy_central silently switching away from a fixed-truth bilinear fold to any other combining law with a different value on this fixture (e.g. a replica second moment) -- demonstrated distinguishable, 7-8% apart. Does NOT catch: an index-transposed contraction (einsum 'rji,ij->r' vs 'rij,ij->r') or a field_A/field_B swap inside dy_central, because outer(truth['q'], truth['q']) is symmetric when field_A==field_B -- demonstrated: both mutants reproduce the correct value exactly on this fixture. Also does not catch a wrong nu or wrong basis threaded to bilinear_tensor, since the stub kernel ignores both arguments.

weaknesses.evidence: RESOLVED 2026-08-13 by the new test_bilinear_fold_is_index_weight_and_kinematics_faithful. Rather than extending the existing symmetric case (which is kept -- its expected value is readable by inspection), a second test carries a fixture that is asymmetric in every axis under test: a non-symmetric tensor, three contributions with field_A != field_B, distinct truths per field, three distinct non-unit weights, and TWO kernel instances so dy_central's (id(kernel), id(evolution_A), id(evolution_B)) grouping must build two groups and accumulate the first group's two outer products. The stub kernel records its call arguments, so dataset.nu and the shared field basis are asserted to be threaded through rather than ignored. Four assert-not-allclose controls measure that the fixture separates each bug class. Bar rtol=1e-13. Acceptance: in-memory mutations of dy_central implementing (a) einsum('rji,ij->r'), (b) np.outer(curve_B, curve_A), (c) weight=1.0, and (d) a single merged group each make it fail, while test_linear_and_bilinear_generation_fold_the_same_fixed_truth passes under all four -- the recorded finding, demonstrated. tests/test_closure_truth_representable.py:119 (BilinearContribution('q','q',Kernel())) and :123 (expected = einsum('rij,i,j->r', tensor, truth['q'], truth['q'])) -- field_A==field_B=='q' makes outer(truth['q'],truth['q']) symmetric. Measured standalone on the exact fixture: einsum('rji,ij->r', tensor, outer) and einsum('rij,ij->r', tensor, outer(truth_q,truth_q).T) both equal einsum('rij,ij->r', tensor, outer) exactly ([28., 72.1] all three).
weaknesses.why_it_matters: A dy_central that accidentally contracted 'rji,ij->r' instead of 'rij,ij->r', or built outer(curve_B, curve_A) instead of outer(curve_A, curve_B) -- a realistic index-order slip in the real generate.py:513-524 grouping/einsum code -- would pass this test's only bilinear case silently. tests/test_closure_dy_evolution.py almost certainly catches this class for real multi-flavour DY datasets, where field_A != field_B contributions are the norm (see its dy_field_maps-based reference), so this is a gap in this file's own discriminating power, not necessarily in the suite.
weaknesses.proposed_fix: Add a second bilinear case (or extend the fixture) with field_A != field_B and distinct truth values on each side, e.g. BilinearContribution('q', 'g', Kernel()) with truth['q'] != truth['g'], so outer(A, B) is asymmetric and a transposition/swap bug becomes visible.

weaknesses.evidence: RESOLVED 2026-08-13 (no code change needed, as recorded). The per-test docstring and the comment at the closing assertion now state precisely that the line checks the fixture's discriminating power -- that the replica-second-moment law disagrees with the fixed-truth law on this fixture -- rather than calling gen.dy_central a second time. The combined two-assertion mechanism is sound; only the attribution needed correcting. Verified unchanged this pass. tests/test_closure_truth_representable.py:130-142: 'assert not np.allclose(exact, second_moment)' runs after 'exact' was already bound and validated by 'assert_allclose(exact, expected)' two statements earlier (line 124). Given that assertion passed, exact ~= expected, so the closing assert is algebraically equivalent to 'expected != second_moment', a fact about the fixture arrays computed entirely in plain numpy -- it does not call gen.dy_central a second time.
weaknesses.why_it_matters: The pre-edit comment ('cannot be substituted for the fixed function without breaking the truth target') read as if this line itself exercises dy_central against the second-moment law. It does not: it certifies that the earlier assert_allclose had the power to reject that law (a real and useful property -- see measurements), but taken alone a reader could mistake it for an independent second check on the implementation. The combined two-assertion mechanism is sound; only the attribution needed correcting, which the rewritten comment/docstring now does.
weaknesses.proposed_fix: No code change needed. Addressed via the rewritten comment at lines 130-136 and the per-test docstring, which now state precisely that this line checks the fixture's discriminating power rather than calling gen again.

weaknesses.evidence: RESOLVED 2026-08-14 by test_bilinear_fold_uses_the_ensemble_mean_not_the_ensemble_second_moment and test_all_four_dy_central_bodies_are_the_same_source. This is S0-05, closed. closure_*_small/generate.py::dy_central now runs the full suites' fixed-truth fold verbatim (AST-identical across all four packages), the two _small call sites pass mean_curves instead of the replica stack ens, and a new _one_truth_curve helper in ALL FOUR copies REFUSES a non-1-D truth curve rather than letting np.outer flatten it. DY_PACKAGES now parametrizes both bilinear tests over all four packages -- the package-level gap that let the bug live. Acceptance, two independent mutations: (a) the VERBATIM shipped _small dy_central restored on the two _small modules makes exactly the 4 _small parametrizations of the two bilinear tests fail plus the drift guard, while the full-package parametrizations pass (5 failed, 8 passed); (b) a signature-preserving mutation that drops the shape guard and silently reduces a replica stack to its mean makes all 4 parametrizations of the new test fail on DID NOT RAISE (4 failed, 9 passed). Before the fix both new tests passed only on the two full packages. Measured law difference on the shipped ensembles at Q=2: JAM 2.4e-03/2.9e-03, NNPDF 2.1e-03/6.4e-03 max|ratio-1|. ORIGINAL: the two _small packages were excluded from the package parametrization and no test anywhere called their dy_central, so the replica-second-moment law shipped unexercised.
weaknesses.why_it_matters: A closure test exists to check that the fit recovers a known truth. The _small suites wrote the ensemble MEAN to truth.json while generating their DY rows from the ensemble SECOND moment, which no single PDF reproduces -- so DY coverage in those suites was measuring a central value with no truth curve behind it. The fix is truth-kind agnostic: dy_central takes whatever one curve the caller records, so switching between replica_ensemble_mean and fixed_lhapdf_member needs no change here.
weaknesses.proposed_fix: (applied) adopt the full suites' dy_central; parametrize the bilinear tests over all four packages; add a 1-D shape guard.

measurements.claim: closure_JAM_truth_small/closure_NNPDF_truth_small's dy_central formula (C = qA.T @ qB / n_rep, generate.py:265) applied to this test's own 'replicas' array reproduces the test's 'second_moment' value to float precision -- it is the same formula, not merely the same concept.
measurements.command: standalone script: C = replicas.T @ replicas / replicas.shape[0]; small_suite_formula = np.einsum('rij,ij->r', tensor, C, optimize=True); compared against second_moment computed exactly as in the test file
measurements.result: both print [30., 77.7]; max abs diff 1.42e-14; np.allclose(second_moment, small_suite_formula, rtol=1e-12, atol=0) is True

measurements.claim: field_A == field_B == 'q' makes this test's bilinear check blind to an index-transposed contraction and to a field_A/field_B swap inside dy_central.
measurements.command: standalone script: outer = np.outer(truth_q, truth_q); correct = einsum('rij,ij->r', tensor, outer); mutant_transposed = einsum('rji,ij->r', tensor, outer); mutant_swapped = einsum('rij,ij->r', tensor, outer.T)
measurements.result: correct, mutant_transposed and mutant_swapped are all exactly [28., 72.1]; np.allclose(outer, outer.T) is True (outer(q,q) is symmetric by construction)

measurements.claim: The replica-second-moment matrix C = qA.T @ qB / n_rep is not the outer product of any single vector (rank > 1), so it does not correspond to any single 'representable' PDF truth in the sense this file's claim is about.
measurements.command: np.linalg.matrix_rank(replicas.T @ replicas / replicas.shape[0]) on the test's own 2-replica fixture; also inspected C - np.outer(mean, mean)
measurements.result: rank == 2 (an outer(v,v) is always rank <= 1); C - outer(mean,mean) = [[0.25,0.25,0.5],[0.25,0.25,0.5],[0.5,0.5,1.0]], nonzero (the Cov(replicas) term)
